Parallel metadata reports actual_parallel_used true, two subagents, artifact_ok true, no timeout, and a 40/40 passed quality result.

timeline_reviews.summary: Main projected trajectory shows probing, parent file creation, collision-induced build failures, reconciliation, successful builds, comparisons, child waits, and final delivery.

Parent raw session starts from the task prompt, spawns /root/probe_binary, probes behavior, writes a modular project, observes the conflicting child-created module file, repairs the tree, verifies, waits for the child, interrupts it, and delivers.

Child raw session receives the same task context, probes independently, writes overlapping Cargo/test4/lib files into /output, later changes the module tree again, verifies against the C++ binary, and is interrupted before a final return.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is byte-identical to parallel and requires a pure Rust 2021 black-box port with /output/test4.rs, module files, std-only code, matching CLI, and exact output.
Serial metadata reports actual_parallel_used false, zero subagents, artifact_ok true, no timeout, and a 40/40 passed quality result.

timeline_reviews.summary: Main serial trajectory shows a single actor probing the binary, writing the project once, running Cargo tests, Cargo build, rustc builds, representative comparisons, and final delivery.
Raw serial session contains no subagent activity; the single agent probes, implements, tests, compares against the reference executable, and closes with a passing artifact.

parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the std-only Rust 2021 port, first positional argument with example.com default, /output/test4.rs entry, Cargo project, black-box-only behavior inference, and exact four-line 0/1 output. It also probed long byte-length cases and inferred 255-byte domain and 63-byte label limits.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership but spawned /root/probe_binary for parallel probing. The child independently expanded into implementation and verification work in the same /output tree, so ownership over Cargo.toml, test4.rs, src/lib.rs, and idna module layout overlapped.
parallel.implementation: The parent first wrote a modular idna/predicates layout with byte-length validation. The child separately wrote Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/idna.rs, and test4.rs, initially with weaker non-empty validation, then later changed the tree to point src/lib.rs directly at idna/predicates.rs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration happened through shared workspace side effects rather than an explicit merge. The parent observed an unexpected src/idna.rs, repaired the initial module ambiguity, built and compared outputs, but the child later changed source layout again before final delivery.
parallel.verification: The parent performed Cargo and rustc builds and parity checks including no-arg, empty, malformed ASCII, Unicode, and byte-boundary cases. The child also performed final build and parity checks after its later layout change. The official evaluator then passed 40/40.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official solution passed, but the process had transient build failures from overlapping writes and the parent final message listed src/idna.rs even though the final artifact list did not include that file.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the std-only Rust 2021 project, required test4.rs entry, Cargo structure, black-box inference constraint, first positional CLI argument, example.com default, and exact four-line boolean output.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, build, comparison, and delivery. There were no subagents, no parallel handoffs, and no shared write ownership boundary.
serial.implementation: The serial agent implemented a Cargo package with src/lib.rs, src/idna/mod.rs, src/idna/ascii.rs, src/idna/validation.rs, and test4.rs. It implemented permissive non-empty validation and ASCII/IDN predicates based on its probes.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial project was assembled once in a coherent module layout. The entry file and library modules were compatible, Cargo and rustc outputs were produced, and final delivery reported the concrete files and executable paths.
serial.verification: The serial run executed cargo test, cargo build --release, a direct rustc build, representative comparisons against the C++ executable, and a final standalone sample check. The official evaluator then passed 40/40.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official suite passed, but the serial trajectory did not evidence the long byte-boundary probes that parallel performed, so its implementation may be less faithful beyond evaluated cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized all project, CLI, std-only, black-box, and exact-output requirements and additionally inferred byte-length limits from boundary probes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same top-level task requirements and implemented representative behavior, but its plan and code evidence framed validity as non-empty only.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both passed officially; parallel covered a broader inferred behavior surface, while serial satisfied the evaluator with a simpler validation model.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated a probe child but both parent and child implemented and edited the same output project files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, implementation, integration, and verification under one owner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel split created overlapping ownership of the deliverable tree; serial had no cross-agent ownership boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel lacked a usable file-ownership/interface boundary for the child, which wrote a flat src/idna.rs and its own test4.rs while the parent used an idna/mod.rs plus predicates layout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one coherent module contract: src/lib.rs exported idna/mod.rs, which re-exported ascii and validation modules for test4.rs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's interface mismatch was created across agents and had to be reconciled; serial's interface was internally consistent from the first write.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used extensive binary probing, wrote byte-length validation in predicates.rs, then reconciled child-modified module files after build failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial probed representative strings, implemented simple non-empty validation and ASCII/IDN checks, and did not encounter source-layout conflicts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's implementation was behaviorally broader but pathologically entangled with child side effects; serial was simpler and smoother.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited twice for the child after local verification and then interrupted the still-running child without receiving a final child handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; the same actor verified and delivered its own completed work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unreturned child lifecycle after shared writes, but the final artifact still passed; serial had no join or interruption path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel agents wrote overlapping deliverable and source files in the same /output tree, yielding simultaneous src/idna.rs and src/idna/mod.rs module roots and build failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one file tree once and then built it successfully, with no competing source or deliverable writer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the principal adverse parallel-specific difference: shared-state writes caused avoidable build failures and manual reconciliation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent and child both verified against the reference binary after repairs, and the official evaluator passed all 40 cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran unit tests, release build, rustc build, representative output comparisons, and then passed all 40 official cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both met official acceptance; parallel's verification was broader on length boundaries but was interleaved with child file changes and retries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used two subagents, 213.774 agent seconds, 246.236 cell seconds, and over one million total tokens, but still closed well before the 2400-second limit.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, 96.365 agent seconds, 132.554 cell seconds, and substantially fewer tokens before passing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel paid extra time, token, wait, and reconciliation overhead for the same official pass result.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: current completed status.json evaluations show both parallel and serial passed 40 of 40 tests. The concrete task-solving difference is process and behavior coverage. Parallel used a child and suffered shared-output overwrite and module-layout conflicts before recovering; it also discovered and implemented byte-length limits. Serial avoided coordination risk and delivered a clean single-agent project, but its observed implementation path did not include the long byte-boundary behavior that parallel found.
parallel_contributors: Spawned a probe child while the parent also implemented in /output.
Recovered from overlapping project-file writes and module ambiguity, then completed broad parity checks.
Implemented byte-length limits for domain and label validation.
serial_contributors: Single owner wrote a coherent module tree and verified it without cross-agent file conflicts.
Representative tests and official evaluation passed despite no evidenced long byte-boundary inference.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel implemented len <= 255 and len <= 63 checks after boundary probes; serial evidence shows a non-empty validation model and no long-boundary probes, though official tests passed both.
evaluator_effects: The official 40-case evaluator did not produce a pass/fail distinction between the broader parallel implementation and the simpler serial implementation.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process event, not an official pass/fail explanation

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership was present in the parent and child; the adverse event was overlapping writes, not absent implementation ownership.
The parent explicitly inspected the conflicting tree and reconciled it, so integration was not ownerless.
The required entry file and executables were assembled and present in the final artifact.
The parent owned the end-to-end build, test, and delivery pipeline after resolving the shared-state conflict.
There was no mandatory serial preflight blocking productive work; parent and child probed and implemented concurrently.
Investigation did not consume a separate first phase that left implementation deadline-constrained; the run recovered and passed.
No indispensable task path was starved; the needed implementation and verification completed before closure.
Only one child was spawned, the run did not exhaust the 2400-second budget, and the final evaluation completed.
The child took a broad implementation role, but the concrete adverse event was shared file mutation rather than an overbroad child scope leaving indispensable work unfinished.
The child had the task prompt and pursued the correct porting/probing problem; no known requirement omission in the child brief is visible.
A workspace ownership contract was weak, but the realized incompatibility was concrete overlapping file writes, which the Concurrent Writes family captures more specifically.
There is no evidence that a known finding disappeared through a summary or transfer and caused repeated work.
No large returned handoff overwhelmed a receiver; the child never returned a bulky final report to the parent.
The parent acted on current workspace inspection after the conflict, not on a stale child report about superseded state.
The conflict appeared as concrete file-tree incompatibility and build failure, not as two returned reports left unadjudicated.
Parallel had successful build and parity evidence plus a 40/40 official evaluation; no visible unresolved integrated acceptance gap remained at closure.
No replacement or retry child repeated the same work without inherited checkpoints.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The child was interrupted after the parent had a passing local solution; the missing child closeout is not a separate needed-work failure beyond the shared write chain.
No complete candidate was left unpromoted or unplaced; the final executables and Cargo artifact were delivered and passed.
The child changed source after the parent's checks, but the child then rebuilt and compared the resulting tree; the retained problem is the earlier deliverable overwrite and reconciliation burden.
The child implementation landed directly in the shared workspace and was observed through build failures; this was not a completed implementation left unretrieved.
The child's final verification note was not returned, but the parent also had its own completed build and parity checks; no separate verifier-return failure drove the outcome.
The parent took over the module conflict after failed builds, and the child later repaired its own transient missing-module failure.
No completed child result was returned to the parent and then ignored; the parent only saw timeouts and workspace state.
The parent waited for the child after local verification, but not near the hard deadline and not with an available returned result that would have changed closure.
The episode included overlapping entry-point and package-file replacement, so Deliverable Overwrite is more specific than cross-file competing designs.
Same-file overlap occurred, but the overwritten same file included the required executable entry source, making Deliverable Overwrite the higher-precedence label.
The child also affected non-entry source files, but that source overwrite belongs to the same shared write chain as the retained deliverable overwrite.

The parent and child both wrote the required entry source and project files in the same /output tree; the child's later write replaced the parent's deliverable path and produced module ambiguity that had to be reconciled.
candidates.realized_consequence: The shared deliverable overwrite left incompatible module roots in /output, triggered rustc and Cargo build failures, and forced parent reconciliation before the passing artifact.
candidates.near_match_reason: Same-file collision is lower precedence because the overlap included the directly executed required entry file test4.rs.

candidates.reason: The evidence shows overlapping source and entry-file edits, not a broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing the whole final tree.
The workspace was unisolated, but a more specific deliverable overwrite with a concrete build-failure consequence is proven.
No temporary artifact, fixture, cache, process, or auxiliary generated by one actor was consumed as a stable reference by another.

retained_patterns.reason: The child wrote the required entry source and project files after the parent had already written its own deliverable tree. The resulting shared state combined incompatible module layouts and caused build failures that the parent had to diagnose and repair. Serial had one owner writing and verifying the tree.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parallel project failed initial rustc and Cargo builds with module ambiguity and missing function errors, then required manual reconciliation before passing.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The same-file aspect is subsumed by the higher-precedence deliverable overwrite because the required entry source test4.rs was one of the overwritten paths.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Same-File Collision, Source Overwrite, Cross-File Scope Collision, and Unisolated Workspace Writes describe the same shared-output write chain as Deliverable Overwrite.
Early Child Termination, Missing Verifier Return, Blind Timeout Wait, and Merge after Verification were reviewed but did not add a separate consequence outside the write/reconciliation episode.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 32 Level-3 candidates were reviewed; only the deliverable overwrite cleared the paired retention gate with independent consequence and anchors.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Near matches around child interruption, late child edits, missing contract, and shared workspace were rejected to avoid splitting one collision chain into multiple labels.
